format_scores.reason: The 'boring correct decisions' mechanic maps cleanly onto Notion's pain — using Notion instead of five scattered apps is exactly the kind of unglamorous discipline habit that slots into this list naturally, and the self-deprecating tone matches Notion's calm/clever register without needing much bending.

The red-flag checklist mechanic maps naturally onto Notion's pain point - each 'red flag' can be a recognizable symptom of the tab-drowning, multi-app chaos (e.g., 'keeps your docs in a Slack thread', 'sends you a Google Doc that links to a Jira that links to a spreadsheet'), and the green-flag payoff flips cleanly to Notion without pitching directly, matching the calm/clever tone well with only minor bending needed to frame a workspace tool in dating-vetting language.

The mechanic fits well because the gap between an ambitious claim and the mundane reality (e.g., 'thought I could reorganize the entire company's knowledge base' → 'asked Notion AI where that one doc was' → 'actually found it') maps directly onto the core pain of drowning in tabs and the hard way of juggling five apps, and Notion's calm/clever tone pairs naturally with deadpan self-awareness without needing much bending.

The escalating negation list maps reasonably well to the 'drowning in tabs' pain and the hard way of copying between five apps — you can slot in Google Docs, Slack, Jira, Confluence as the negated alts — but the 'admired for refusing the easy path' mechanic slightly misfires because Notion IS the easy path, not the scrappy last resort, so the 'psychopath' framing has to be bent to make the chaos-embracer the subject rather than the Notion user.
